title: ⚡ Grammar Mastery Test

sections.heading: Instructions
sections.body:
This test covers all grammar structures from this unit: complex sentences, relative clauses, passive voice, conditionals, reported speech, inversion, nominalization, hedging, and discourse markers.

You need 80% to achieve "Grammar Mastery" status.

highlight: This is the hardest test in the course. Every question targets a different grammar structure. Take your time.

question: Which sentence uses PASSIVE VOICE correctly?
options: The research has conducted by scientists.
The research was conducted by scientists.
correct: The research was conducted by scientists.
explanation:
Past simple passive: WAS/WERE + past participle
"The research WAS CONDUCTED by scientists" ✅

❌ "conducted by" with no auxiliary = incomplete
❌ "has conducted" = present perfect ACTIVE
❌ "were conducted the research" = nonsensical structure

question: Which sentence correctly uses INVERSION after a negative adverb?
options: Never I have witnessed such a transformation.
Never have I witnessed such a transformation.
I have never witnessed such a transformation.
Never witnessed have I such a transformation.
correct: Never have I witnessed such a transformation.
explanation:
Inversion pattern: NEGATIVE ADVERB + AUXILIARY + SUBJECT + MAIN VERB
Never HAVE I WITNESSED ✅

Standard position: I have NEVER witnessed (no inversion)

question: Which correctly nominalizes the verb "decide"?
explanation:
"Decision" is the correct nominalization of "decide".

"Decidement" — not a word
"The deciding" — gerund, not standard nominalization
"The decided" — adjective used as noun, ungrammatical here

sentence: _______ the government _______ invested more in renewable energy earlier, the current energy crisis might _______ been avoided.
explanation:
Type 3 conditional inversion: HAD + subject + past participle... MIGHT HAVE + past participle

Full sentence: "Had the government invested more... the crisis might have been avoided"

This combines inversion (Had) + Type 3 conditional + modal perfect (might have been) — a Band 9 structure.
